extracted.intended_audience: Training PD/PIs, applicant organizations, authorized organizational representatives, and grants administrators preparing Kirschstein-NRSA (T32/T35/T34) institutional research training grant applications
extracted.subtask_description: Preparation and administration of Kirschstein‑NRSA institutional research training grant (e.g., T32/T35/T34) applications and programs, including eligibility, program design, review criteria, trainee appointment/terms, and post‑award requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple PD/PIs — Leadership Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications reflecting multiple PD/PIs must provide a Leadership Plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis should be on how it will benefit the research training program and the trainees. Additional information required includes structure and governance of the PD/PI leadership team. Multiple PD/PI applications should include reasonable numbers of PD/PIs; each individual should be included for a specific purpose and programs should not list all mentors as PD/PIs except in unusual cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple PD/PIs — Contact PD/PI designation
rubrics_metrics.description: A single Contact PD/PI must be designated for communication with NIH.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although others may contact NIH on behalf of the Contact PD/PI when necessary, only a single award will be issued and NIH will not allocate budget or training positions between multiple PD/PIs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of Research Training Program
rubrics_metrics.description: Kirschstein-NRSA institutional research training grants must be used to support a program of research training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May not support studies leading to clinical professional degrees except as part of a formal combined research degree (e.g., M.D./Ph.D.). Trainees may not accept NRSA support for clinical training that is part of residency leading to clinical certification, though clinicians may undertake full‑time postdoctoral research training even if creditable toward specialty certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trainee Full‑time Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Research trainees are expected to devote full time to the proposed research training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full‑time is generally defined as at least 40 hours per week or as specified by the sponsoring institution. Clinician‑trainees must confine clinical duties to those integral to the research training experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predoctoral Eligibility and Degree Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Predoctoral training is for individuals with a baccalaureate (or equivalent) enrolled in a program leading to a Ph.D. or comparable research doctoral degree or a combined clinical degree and Ph.D.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individuals who already hold research or professional doctoral degrees (e.g., Ph.D., M.D., D.D.S., etc.) are not eligible for predoctoral training. Students in integrated dual‑degree programs (e.g., M.D./Ph.D.) maintain predoctoral status while enrolled; a student cannot simultaneously hold predoctoral and postdoctoral status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postdoctoral Eligibility and Degree Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Postdoctoral research training is for individuals who have received an eligible doctoral degree (Ph.D., M.D., D.D.S., etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipient institution determines foreign degree equivalence. Postdoctoral training must emphasize specialized training to meet national research priorities. Health‑professional postdocs should engage in at least two years of research or comparable experiences beginning at appointment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short‑Term Research Training (T32/T35) — Purpose & Duration
rubrics_metrics.description: Short‑term research training provides full‑time 2–3 month experiences for health‑professional students and select quantitative science students under T32 or via T35.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short‑term appointments should last at least 8 but no more than 12 weeks. Positions intended to attract health‑professional students into research careers; applicants should request short‑term positions in application. Contact relevant ICs as not all ICs support short‑term positions under T32.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short‑Term Training — Eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible for short‑term predoctoral positions, students must be enrolled and in good standing and have completed at least one quarter or semester in a qualifying program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individuals already matriculated in a formal research degree program, holding a research doctorate or master's, or combined professional/research doctorates normally are not eligible. In pharmacy schools, only Pharm.D. candidates are eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre‑baccalaureate Training (T34)
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH offers pre‑baccalaureate training under the Kirschstein‑NRSA undergraduate support mechanism (T34).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs are designed to support selected students at various institutions; specific program information is available in applicable NOFOs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citizenship/Residency Eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Trainees must be U.S. citizens, noncitizen nationals, or lawful permanent residents at time of appointment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permanent residents must have valid Form I‑551 or other legal verification; notarized copy of passport with validation may suffice temporarily (6‑month limit). Conditional permanent residents may be supported but recipient must ensure continued eligibility. Asylum/refugee status alone is not sufficient; temporary or student visa holders are not eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Submission Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: All applications are submitted electronically through Grants.gov using SF424 (R&R) application package combined with PHS398 components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must follow NOFO‑specific instructions and SF424(R&R) Application Guide; pay particular attention to special instructions for institutional research training grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Receipt Dates and Consultation
rubrics_metrics.description: IC‑specific receipt dates vary; some ICs have three cycles per year while others use one or two.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult Grants.gov NOFOs or contact the appropriate NIH IC program official. Applicants are encouraged to contact NIH staff before preparing and submitting applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Program Considerations — Duration and Transition
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider duration of training and trainees' transition to individual support mechanisms and next career stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PD/PIs should appoint individuals committed to research who plan to remain on the training grant or in other research experiences for a minimum aggregate of 2 years. Training should include preparation for applying to individual fellowships, K awards, or independent grants. Peer reviewers will examine average duration of appointments and history of transition to individual support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ongoing Evaluation of Training Program Quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Training PD/PIs must develop methods for ongoing evaluation of the quality and effectiveness of the training program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plans should include obtaining feedback from current and former trainees to identify weaknesses and suggestions for improvement, and assessing trainee career development (publications, degree completion, post‑training positions). Evaluation results must be included in renewal applications and Final RPPR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruitment and Diversity Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Attention must be given to recruiting prospective trainees from all backgrounds in biomedical, behavioral, and clinical sciences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Per 42 USC 288(a)(4), the program must be carried out to recruit women and individuals from disadvantaged backgrounds (including racial and ethnic minorities) and provide research training to such individuals; individuals of all backgrounds are encouraged to participate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required Plan for Training in Responsible Conduct of Research (RCR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every trainee supported by an NRSA training grant must receive instruction in the responsible conduct of research and all applications must include a plan addressing five components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Renewal applications must describe changes and future plans. All training faculty who contributed to RCR instruction during the past period must be named. Applications lacking an RCR plan will be considered incomplete and may be delayed; plans and past records will be rated acceptable or unacceptable; unacceptable plans must be revised before funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCR — Format
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion‑based instruction with substantive face‑to‑face interaction among participants and faculty is expected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Video conferencing may be incorporated provided it fosters discussion, active learning, and interaction; video conferencing should not be the sole means except in special short‑term programs or well‑justified circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCR — Subject Matter Topics
rubrics_metrics.description: RCR instruction should include a range of substantive topics that reflect developments in research conduct and the broader research environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Topics include: conflict of interest and commitment; human subjects, vertebrate animals, and lab safety policies; mentor/trainee responsibilities and relationships; safe research environments (free of discrimination/harassment); collaborative research including industry and international collaborations; peer review confidentiality; data acquisition/analysis and recordkeeping (e.g., electronic lab notebooks); secure and ethical data use, management, sharing, and ownership; research misconduct and handling policies; responsible authorship/publication; and the scientist's societal responsibilities and environmental/societal impacts of research.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCR — Faculty Participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Training faculty and sponsors/mentors should contribute to both formal and informal RCR instruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Informal instruction occurs in lab interactions; faculty may serve as discussion leaders, speakers, lecturers, or course directors. Rotating faculty roles can help achieve broad faculty participation over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCR — Duration
rubrics_metrics.description: Instruction should involve substantive contact hours between trainees and participating faculty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable programs generally involve at least eight contact hours. Semester‑long series may be more effective than a single seminar or one‑day workshop to allow depth and synthesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCR — Frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: RCR instruction should be undertaken at least once during each career stage and at a frequency of no less than once every four years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions are encouraged to provide ongoing and discipline‑specific training tailored to career stage; advanced students/postdocs may receive more tailored, discipline-specific RCR training if they previously had broad instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCR Reporting Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Information on the nature of RCR instruction and extent of trainee/faculty participation must be provided in the annual progress report for non‑competing continuation support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer Review — Overall Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers provide an overall impact score reflecting likelihood that the research training program will exert a sustained, powerful influence on the research fields involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scored review criteria and additional criteria (as applicable) are considered in determining overall impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scored Review Criteria — Training Program and Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will give a separate score for the Training Program and Environment in assessing scientific and technical merit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NOFO should be consulted for additional information describing this scored criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scored Review Criteria — Training Program Director/Principal Investigator
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will give a separate score for the Training Program Director/Principal Investigator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Knowledge, skills, and experience of PD/PIs are factored into assessment of overall scientific merit; NOFO provides further detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scored Review Criteria — Preceptor/Mentors
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will give a separate score for the quality and appropriateness of Preceptors/Mentors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NOFO should be consulted for additional information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scored Review Criteria — Trainees
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will give a separate score for the Trainees (selection, qualifications, and support).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NOFO provides additional guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scored Review Criteria — Training Record
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will give a separate score for the Training Record of the program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer reviewers will examine history of trainees' durations and transitions to individual support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Review Criteria (considered but not separately scored)
rubrics_metrics.description: As applicable, reviewers will consider protections for human subjects; inclusion of women, minorities, and individuals across the lifespan; vertebrate animals; biohazards; training in methods for enhancing reproducibility; and application resubmission/renewal/revision status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These items are considered in scientific and technical merit determinations but will not receive separate numeric scores; consult NOFO for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Review Considerations (not scored; not part of overall impact)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will address, as applicable, items including Training in RCR, Select Agents Research, and Budget and Period of Support, but should not give scores for these items and should not consider them in the overall impact score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the NOFO for additional information describing these considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Advisory Council Second‑Level Review
rubrics_metrics.description: Following initial peer review, applications undergo second‑level review by the appropriate IC National Advisory Council/Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Council will consider the peer review group's assessment of scientific/educational merit and comments on the RCR plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of Action and Post‑Review Communication
rubrics_metrics.description: PD/PI will be emailed when SRG recommendation/impact score and summary statement are available in eRA Commons; PO may notify PD/PI of final review recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once administrative and programmatic issues are resolved, the Notice of Award will be issued for selected applications. Questions about review recommendations/funding should be directed to the assigned PO, not the SRO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training Grant Period of Support
rubrics_metrics.description: Kirschstein‑NRSA institutional training grants may be awarded for competitive segments up to 5 years and are renewable; awards within a competitive segment are normally made in 12‑month budget periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support for additional non‑competitive years depends on satisfactory progress, submission of required trainee documents, and availability of funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trainee Appointment Length and Timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Trainees generally are appointed for full‑time 12‑month continuous periods and an appointment may begin any time during the budget period but not before the budget period start date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An appointment may not exceed 12 months without prior NIH awarding IC approval. Except for short‑term positions, no trainee may be appointed for less than 9 months without prior written approval (usually only to complete an ongoing training program). Initial appointments shorter than 9 months may be allowed if assurance of immediate reappointment to reach at least 9 months is included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part‑Time Training Approval Conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Part‑time training is allowable only with a written request to the awarding IC signed by trainee, AOR, and PD/PI providing justification and expected duration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests considered case‑by‑case for reasons such as medical conditions, disability, or personal/family situations. Part‑time training will not be approved to accommodate other funding sources, job opportunities, clinical practice, or other responsibilities. Request must include estimate of duration and assurances trainee intends to return to full‑time training. Stipend may be prorated and part‑time may affect payback accrual/repayment. Trainees must not be below 50% effort; under 50% requires leave of absence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregate NRSA Support Limitations and Waiver Process
rubrics_metrics.description: No individual may receive more than 5 years aggregate NRSA support at predoctoral level and 3 years at postdoctoral level (including institutional and individual awards).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions require written waiver request from the AOR to the awarding IC with endorsement from PD/PI; generally favorable categories include physicians/clinicians needing extra time, interruptions (e.g., loss of preceptor, illness), or other exceptional justifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initiation of Support — Required Forms at Appointment
rubrics_metrics.description: At initial appointment and reappointment, PD/PI must submit a Statement of Appointment (PHS Form 2271) and, for postdocs in their first 12 months, a signed Payback Agreement (PHS Form 6031).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Statement of Appointment includes trainee biographical data and stipend level. Stipend is paid by recipient organization directly to trainee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable and Unallowable Costs — Pre‑award Costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost principles in 2 CFR Part 200 Subpart E and NIHGPS govern training grant expenditures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stipends and tuition/fees may not be charged to a grant as pre‑award costs until a trainee has been officially appointed and required paperwork submitted; rare exceptions exist and institutions should consult the awarding IC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stipend Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Stipends are subsistence allowances (not salary) and must be paid in accordance with established NIH stipend levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions may hire trainees as employees or provide benefits but should consult IRS. Recipient organizations may not negotiate NIH stipend amounts with trainees; NIH stipend amounts may be adjusted only at appointment or reappointment. For postdocs, stipend level is set by number of full years of relevant postdoctoral experience at appointment and must remain at that level for the grant year. Appointments shorter than 12 months are prorated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trainee Tuition and Fees Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Tuition and fees are allowable only if applied consistently to all individuals in similar training status regardless of funding source; postdoc tuition limited to required courses with prior IC approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Predoctoral: NIH provides an amount equal to 60% of institutional actual tuition up to $16,000/year (up to $21,000/year for combined dual‑degree programs). Postdoctoral: 60% of actual tuition up to $4,500/year (or up to $16,000/year if enrolled in a formal degree‑granting postdoctoral program). Tuition/fees are awarded as a lump sum that may be allocated without prior approval.
